title: Goodbye, please and sorry
goal: Say goodbye, please, sorry and OK, and spell the letters ş and ň.

intro.text: The one who leaves says *Hoş gal* (goodbye; literally “stay well”), and the one who stays can answer *Ak ýol!* (have a good trip). *Haýyş edýärin* is **please**, *Bagyşlaň* is **excuse me** or **sorry**, and *Bolýar* is **OK**. *ş* is the sh of “ship”; *ň* the ng of “sing”.

vocab.en: have a good trip (said to the one leaving)

exercises.question: Merjen is leaving, and you are staying. What does Merjen say to you?

why.1: *Ak ýol!* (literally “white road”) is what **you** say to Merjen: have a good trip.

exercises.explain: The one who leaves says *Hoş gal*, “stay well”. The one who stays can answer *Ak ýol!* or *Sag bol!*
*Bagyşlaň* ends in *ň*, the ng of “sing”. Without the mark it is a different sound, so it counts as a spelling mistake.

why.1: That is *s*, which many speakers say like the th of “thin”.

exercises.explain: *Bagyşlaň* is polite, for a stranger or for several people; *bagyşla* is for a friend.

exercises.question: Which is spelled right?

why.1: In *edýärin* the y of “yes” comes before a vowel, so it is the consonant *ý*.
why.2: In *haýyş*, the letter after a is the consonant *ý*; the vowel of the second syllable is *y*.

exercises.explain: *haýyş* has both letters: the consonant *ý* after a, then the vowel *y*.

exercises.question: Your teacher asks you to wait a minute. How do you say **OK**?

reject.why: Before a vowel, the y of “yes” is written *ý*: *edýärin*.

exercises.explain: *Haýyş edýärin* is literally “I make a request”.

exercises.question: You are seeing a friend off at the bus station. What do you say as the bus leaves?

why.1: *Hoş gal* is said by the one who leaves, not by the one who stays.

exercises.explain: *Ak ýol!*, literally “white road”, wishes someone a good journey.
